description:
It's a two-way exchange: information flows not only from scientists to humanitarians, but also from practitioners and communities back to tech developers.

The project purpose is to bridge that connection: bringing people closer to NASA, while bringing NASA closer to people.
summary:
CODE: LEGACY – Every Mission Leaves an Echo

CODE: LEGACY is a screen-free educational card game that brings the stories of NASA’s forgotten space explorers back to life. It transforms the histories of 13 selected spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific missions across the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space into an engaging, story-driven learning experience.
Instead of memorising disconnected facts, players collect four interconnected cards: Identity, Mission, Discovery, and Legacy; to reconstruct how each explorer was designed, why it was sent, what science it enabled, and what remains of its mission. Through a simple, Mahjong-inspired draw-and-discard mechanic, players compete to complete a collection and retell the explorer’s story.

Designed with two age-adapted editions for learners aged 8+ and 13+, CODE: LEGACY makes authentic space science more accessible without requiring prior STEM knowledge. By turning overlooked mission histories into stories that children can discover, connect, and share, the project aims to inspire curiosity about the scientific achievements that shape humanity’s future in space.
details:
CODE: LEGACY is a physical educational card game featuring 13 selected space explorers from lunar and Mars exploration to asteroid missions and deep-space observation.

Each explorer is represented by four interconnected cards:

  • Identity: What is it, and where did it go?
  • Mission: Why was it sent, and how did it work?
  • Discovery: What did it discover or achieve?
  • Legacy: What remains, and why does its story matter?

The game contains 104 cards, comprising 52 unique designs with two copies each. Using a simple, Mahjong-inspired draw-and-discard mechanic, 2-4 players compete to collect four cards belonging to the same explorer. The first player to complete a collection must retell the explorer's story using the cards, while others follow along and verify the key facts. Winning therefore requires both strategic play and the ability to connect the information into a coherent narrative.

Educational Value and Accessibility

Rather than presenting isolated facts or using space merely as a fictional theme, CODE: LEGACY makes authentic mission histories the foundation of its gameplay. It connects each explorer's engineering, purpose, operations, scientific discoveries, and lasting contributions into an accessible story.

The game offers two age-adapted editions: Explorer Edition (ages 8+), with simpler language and visual storytelling, and Investigator Edition (ages 13+), with deeper scientific explanations and technical context. No prior STEM knowledge is required.

Creativity and Intended Impact

The project's central innovation is combining competitive card collection with storytelling. Players do not simply memorise information; they actively reconstruct and retell the history of forgotten space explorers, turning gameplay into a social learning experience.

Beyond the card game, we envision the annual CODE: LEGACY – Echo Challenge, inviting young players to submit videos connecting an explorer's legacy to future space exploration. We also propose distributing decks to schools and reinvesting sales revenue to support under-resourced communities, with a digital edition as a future expansion.

Development Tools and Technology

The current prototype is a physical card game, developed through illustrated card designs, a printed deck, and a player's guide. It requires no specialised hardware or programming, making it suitable for classrooms, libraries, families, and screen-free learning environments.
